# pubmedR

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/pubmedR)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pubmedR)
[![CRAN downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/pubmedR)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=pubmedR)
[![Project Status: Active](https://www.repostatus.org/badges/latest/active.svg)](https://www.repostatus.org/#active)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/massimoaria/pubmedR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/massimoaria/pubmedR/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**pubmedR** downloads bibliographic records from [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) through the NCBI API and turns them into a data frame ready for analysis in R. The data frame uses the field tags of [bibliometrix](https://www.bibliometrix.org), so you can pass it straight to that package and to its Biblioshiny app.

## Installation

```r
# The released version, from CRAN
install.packages("pubmedR")

# The development version, from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("massimoaria/pubmedR")
```

The API is free and needs no key. Without one, NCBI allows 3 requests per second; with a [free API key](https://account.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/settings/) it allows 10. To use a key in every session, add `PUBMED_API_KEY=your_key` to your `.Renviron` file (`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens it).

## Quick start

`pmCollect()` builds the query, downloads the records and converts them in one call:

```{r collect, results='hide'}
library(pubmedR)

M <- pmCollect(
  terms = "bibliometric*",
  language = "english",
  pub_type = "Review",
  date_range = c("2020", "2024"),
  limit = 5
)
```

```{r collect-show}
knitr::kable(M[, c("PY", "TI", "SO")], row.names = FALSE)
```

## Step by step

For more control, run each step yourself. `pmQueryBuild()` writes the query, or you can write your own in the [PubMed search syntax](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/help/#search-tags):

```{r query}
query <- pmQueryBuild(
  terms = c("machine learning", "deep learning"),
  operator = "OR",
  mesh_terms = "Neoplasms",
  language = c("english", "italian"),
  date_range = c("2022", "2024")
)
query
```

Check how many records it finds before downloading them, and see how they spread over the years:

```{r count}
pmQueryTotalCount(query)$total_count

pmCountByYear(query, years = 2022:2024)
```

Then download the records and convert them:

```{r download, results='hide'}
D <- pmApiRequest(query, limit = 20)
M <- pmApi2df(D)
```

```{r download-show}
dim(M)
```

PubMed serves at most 9,999 records per search. If you ask for more, `pmApiRequest()` splits the query by the date records were added to PubMed and downloads the parts in turn. The records then come in that order, newest first, not in the order of the original search.

## Records you already know

Download records by PMID or by DOI. `pmFetchByDoi()` also tells you which DOIs are not in PubMed:

```{r by-id, results='hide'}
by_pmid <- pmFetchById(c("10171110", "25824007"))

known <- pmApi2df(by_pmid)

by_doi <- pmFetchByDoi(c("10.1038/nature14539", "10.9999/not.a.real.doi"))
```

```{r by-id-show}
knitr::kable(known[, c("PMID", "PY", "TI")], row.names = FALSE)

by_doi$not_found
```

## Citations

PubMed records carry no citation count, so `TC` is 0 after the download. There are two sources for it. PubMed counts only the citing articles in PubMed Central, and NIH iCite draws on a larger collection, so its counts are usually higher:

```{r icite}
pmCitedBy("10171110")$count

pmICite("10171110")[, c("pmid", "citation_count", "relative_citation_ratio")]
```

`pmEnrichCitations()` fills in `TC`, along with the cited references (`CR`) and their number (`NR`), for a whole data frame. Pass the downloaded records as `P` to avoid fetching them again:

```{r enrich, results='hide'}
M <- pmEnrichCitations(M, P = D, tc_source = "icite", resolve_pmids = FALSE)
```

```{r enrich-show}
head(M[, c("PY", "TC", "NR")])
```

To list the references of one article, use `pmReferences()` or, for all the records you downloaded, `pmExtractReferences()`.

## Analysis with bibliometrix

```r
library(bibliometrix)

M <- convert2df(D, dbsource = "pubmed", format = "api")
results <- biblioAnalysis(M)
summary(results, k = 10)

# Or work in the app, which can also download from PubMed
biblioshiny()
```

## Main fields

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `AU`, `AF` | Authors, as surname and initials or in full |
| `TI`, `AB` | Title and abstract |
| `SO`, `JI`, `J9` | Journal, and its abbreviation |
| `PY` | Publication year |
| `DT`, `PT` | The first publication type, and all of them |
| `DE`, `ID`, `MESH` | Author keywords and MeSH terms |
| `C1`, `AU_UN` | Affiliations |
| `DI`, `PMID`, `PMCID` | Identifiers |
| `TC`, `CR`, `NR` | Citations, cited references and their number, after enrichment |

## Citation and help

To cite the package, run `citation("pubmedR")`. Report bugs or ask for features in the [issues](https://github.com/massimoaria/pubmedR/issues).
